After an extreme completed loss in a signed-down path, a rebound may be more tradeable when the loss was not accompanied by unusually high causal volume.
Signed-down state; bottom-20% prior loss; next-open entry; 20-session hold; veto causal abnormal volume at or above the 60th percentile.
Broad asset and sector separation plus severity-matched TRAIN separation; the frozen cross-sectional veto gates passed.
Temporal support is unstable: only 3 of 6 years support the veto and 2023 reverses.
Decide whether a genuinely new stabilizing hypothesis is worth a separately frozen test; do not rescue this rule with more post-hoc filters.
A positive completed 20-session return inside causal ER20-sideways was hypothesized to precede executable continuation.
The final mechanism attribution separated positive and negative R20 at the inherited 20-session horizon under the same next-open clock.
Positive R20 trailed negative R20 by 15-19 bp. Only the negative-prior branch cleared drift under both primary lenses.
The continuation sign was wrong; the 20-day horizon was data-informed in the same TRAIN sample. Rebound evidence belongs to a separate research identity.
Set this line down. Do not rescue it by reversing the sign, changing ER20, selecting 20 days, or importing results from the separate rebound line.
After a negative completed 20-session return, an inefficient sideways path may identify a better rebound environment than negative return alone.
At close t require R20 < 0 and ER20 < 0.30; enter open t+1; exit after 20 held sessions; ignore overlap; charge 10 bp. Compare with negative-only, trending-negative, sideways-only, and drift.
Primary excess was +5.8 bp equal-sector and +3.7 bp pooled with 7/11 positive sectors, but incremental lift versus negative-only disagreed by weighting lens (-5.6/+4.3 bp).
Only 2/6 TRAIN years had positive primary excess. The ER20-sideways gate did not robustly improve on negative R20 alone; horizon and cutoff are data-informed.
Huddle before any new calculation. Do not add severity, tune ER20 or the 20-day horizon, select sectors or years, or open post-2023 OOS.

Does multi-session aggregation reveal signed dependence hidden by 1x1 noise?
Weak coherent positive ridge near 5-10 sessions; maximum Pearson about +0.092; no signed-return or direction cell survives the 81-cell scan.
No edge, selected cell, or rule was earned.
Can volatility state conceal opposing return dependence?
LOW and MEDIUM surfaces were positive; HIGH was predominantly negative. Three MEDIUM cells survived the strict 486-test BH family, but the same sample motivated and evaluated the view.
Volatility state became a credible discriminator.
No trading permission or fresh replication was opened.
Can one frozen method discriminate multiple behaviors across assets?
Gain continuation appeared as a smaller cluster, especially in ER20-sideways and low-ATR states; gain exhaustion was broader in efficient/trending states.
The method became an asset-agnostic behavioral vocabulary.
The gain branch remained weaker than the loss-rebound branch.
129 instruments; 15x15 grid; nine states; both signs
Does the gain-branch state split persist with breadth and longer horizons?
ER20-sideways gain cells had median correlation +0.027 and positive sign in 81.8% of cells; ER20-trending had median -0.028 and positive sign in 27.6%.
Sideways continuation versus trending exhaustion became the clearest continuation contrast.
No best cell, candidate rule, or OOS claim was selected.
Does the closed-close rebound geometry survive a next-open rule?
The rule remained heterogeneous and did not justify asset-agnostic deployment; it became a proto-strategy laboratory rather than an edge.
A concrete rule and executable clock were established.
Can causal abnormal volume separate rebound environments without severity confounding?
All seven cross-sectional TRAIN gates passed, but only 3 of 6 years supported the veto and 2023 reversed.
The cross-sectional mechanism became more legible.
Temporal promotion and OOS remained closed.
Is positive-prior continuation more pronounced in causal ER20-sideways than ER20-trending states?
Paired median contrast +0.048; 92.9% of cells favor sideways; all 11 sectors have positive median contrasts. Sixteen cells are exceptions.
The earlier state split became an explicit paired, sector-balanced contrast with visible exceptions.
No horizon, next-open rule, baseline, independent confirmation, or post-2023 outcome was opened.

Does positive R20 inside causal ER20-sideways translate into a next-open continuation rule that improves on matched controls and unconditional drift?

Raw net returns were positive at all holds, but excess versus drift was -16/-10/-14 bp. Only 20d beat trending under both aggregation lenses (+38/+5 bp); the positive-R20 condition underperformed sideways-only at every hold.
The descriptive lead became an auditable open-to-open proto-rule with a visible clock, costs, overlap policy, matched controls, and sector-balanced readout.
No horizon was selected; thresholds were not tuned; portfolio replay, post-2023 OOS, and 30-minute data remain sealed.
129 visible instruments; 88-stock equal-sector core; 2018-2023 TRAIN; one frozen 20-session hold
Is the prior 20-day sideways-state result continuation, negative-prior rebound, a general sideways effect, or a relative morphology artifact?
Only sideways negative-R20 cleared drift under both primary lenses (+5.8/+3.7 bp). Positive-R20 trailed negative-R20 by 15-19 bp; 7/11 sector medians supported the negative branch.
The mechanism changed identity: the continuation interpretation was falsified and a modest, sector-broad rebound lead became visible.
No rebound rule was selected; the 20-day horizon was not retuned; post-2023 OOS, portfolio replay, and 30-minute data remain sealed.
Should the negative-prior result be used to reverse or rescue the continuation hypothesis?
No. Positive R20 was the wrong sign; the continuation interpretation is stopped and the rebound observation receives a separate identity.
The hypothesis ledger now preserves a clean conceptual boundary between continuation and mean reversion.
No sign reversal, rule rescue, horizon selection, or OOS authority was granted.
